title: Canonical SUT adapter manifest (bundle.sut-manifest/v1)
description: A versioned declaration of one System Under Test the Bundle is verified against: how it is resolved, started, reset and stopped; what its oracle is and how independent that oracle is from the SUT; which known-pass and known-fail controls exist; which intentional defects it carries; its resource and access boundaries; the capability-matrix row it runs under; and the CI test that proves it. Only SUTs meeting deterministic reset, bounded runtime, an exact or independent oracle, and source availability belong in the canonical set — a manifest is not a place to promote a historical experiment. Validated by bundle/sut_manifests.py; CI fails on drift.

schema.description: Schema identifier. Consumers reject any value whose name or major differs.

id.description: Stable identifier, also the manifest filename stem.

maturity.description: 'canonical' = part of the release gate set. 'reference' = maintained and usable but not gated. 'experimental' = neither.

source.description: How the SUT is located. `sut_paths_key` resolves through BUNDLE_SUT_ROOT rather than any machine-specific absolute path; `in_repository` SUTs need no external checkout at all.

path.description: Repository-relative path for an in-repository SUT.

sut_paths_key.description: Key in generator_trunk/sut_paths.py for a sibling checkout.

revision.description: Pinned revision, or the resolution rule when the checkout floats.

lifecycle.description: Commands, or an explicit statement that a phase is not applicable. An empty string is not permitted: 'not needed' must be said, not implied by silence.

deterministic.description: Whether identical inputs produce identical observable behaviour. A false value must be explained in `caveats`.

reset.description: How state is returned to a known baseline between candidates.

seed.description: How the deterministic seed is supplied, or why none is needed.

kind.description: 'threshold' is the weakest and must state its limits in `independence`.

independence.description: How the oracle is independent of the thing it judges. An oracle that shares an implementation with the SUT must say so plainly rather than imply independence.

controls.description: A SUT with no known-fail control cannot demonstrate that its oracle detects anything.

interaction_only.description: True when the defect only appears under a specific relation, order, or optional event — the class of fault flat construction misses.

access.description: What the SUT and its candidates are permitted to touch. Declared so a policy violation is detectable rather than merely unlikely.

network.description: Empty array = no network access at all.

trusted_artifacts.description: Binary or downloaded inputs whose integrity matters, with their checksums. Empty for a pure-source SUT — which is itself a fact worth recording.

capability_row.description: The capability-matrix coordinates this SUT is gated at. Validated against bundle/capabilities.py, so a manifest cannot claim a combination the registry refuses.

candidate_origin.description: The origin class the operator declares when launching this SUT's scenarios (audit F1).

tier.description: 1 = fast pull-request gate, 2 = critical integration, 3 = scheduled/release evidence.

workflow_gate.description: Stable marker that must occur in .github/workflows/ci.yml for a canonical SUT; a path that merely exists is not CI execution.

caveats.description: Known limitations. Required in spirit for anything less than an exact oracle.
